questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Career opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: The cost of living in Poland is relatively affordable compared to other European countries. Poland's rich history and vibrant culture were significant draws. I have heard that traveling in Poland is incredibly convenient and enjoyable. Poland was relatively undiscovered for me, and I was eager to learn about its unique culture and history. The vibrant Erasmus community provided a strong support network and enriched my experience.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It's very easy. The University of Warsaw (UW) hosts a Zoom meeting to provide all the necessary information. They also send detailed information via email, making it easy to find everything you need.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: A tutor from the European Student Network (ESN) and an orientation by both ESN and the school provide all the necessary information, including how to sign up for classes. They offer excellent assistance upon your arrival, making it easy to settle down.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: It was easy for me since I knew someone. However, ESN recommends something called Pepshousing for finding your own place, which should make the process smoother.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: The city is big, so it can take sometime to get around. During the day there are a lot of options for get around, however at night their are only busses. Uber can be cheap and a good alternative now and then.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: There are dorms, and sounded like from my friends it was easy to find an apartment.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Their website can seem confusing, and the same for join classes.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: UW opens the registration for all students, then its first come, first serve, however they also give you guide you can follow, which is great, however their website is not user friendly.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: UW provides detailed online information, including specific timeslots for various services. You can find out when and where to meet up on campus to get help with registration problems.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Overall, my experience was quite successful. There was one class I didn't get, but I managed to secure all the others.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Be patient, it will solve it self, and their are help from the school or students.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Classes at UW are generally easy, where exams mostly are presentations or written tests that are easy, but this depend on the course. The law facilities at UW are coon, providing a great environment for study. If you're looking for a semester with less stress, UW is a fantastic choice.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: Both

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I took Erasmus courses at the BA level, and they were quite manageable. Generally, you don't need to study beforehand unless specifically asked to. However, it's important to follow the lectures and participate in class activities, as your participation will be assessed. I also took one MA course, which was similar in structure and difficulty to the Erasmus courses.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: It's a mix of self study and team work, just like UCPH.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Applied Criminology
Civil Law I, Part 1
Comparative Criminal Justice
Emerging Sustainable Development Law
European Legal Tradition
Polish Constitutionalism

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
Comparative Criminal Justice - Sweet teacher, interesting debates and you learn a lot. Exam is a presentation and paper of 3 pages. You choose the topic yourself. 

Applied Criminology - A class trip to visit a polish prison. Interesting topic and the exam is a presentation.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Sports and language classes are available, providing great opportunities to stay active and learn new skills. Additionally, the ESN hosts events outside of school hours, which are fantastic for making new friends and socializing.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: ESN activies!!

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer:
Zakopane: Perfect for outdoor enthusiasts with great skiing in winter and hiking in summer.
Gdańsk: A beautiful coastal city with rich maritime history and stunning architecture.
Kraków: Known for its medieval core, vibrant culture, and historic sites and auschwitz: A somber, important historical site near Kraków, offering a powerful experience. 

During the weekends in Warsaw please visit the museums. They are really good.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: It was easy to settle in. People were very open-minded, kind, and welcoming.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Attend most of the events organized by ESN; that's where you'll meet your friends.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: One cultural difference I found challenging in Poland was the direct communication style. People are very straightforward, which can sometimes feel blunt if you're not used to it.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: I loved Polish cuisine, especially pierogi and bigos. The strong family values and hospitality made me feel welcome, and the vibrant arts scene was inspiring. The warmth and generosity of the Polish people left a lasting impression on me.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: The University of Warsaw has a vibrant student community. Join clubs, attend events, and make connections with both local and international students. This will enhance your experience and help you build lasting friendships. While many people in Warsaw speak English, learning some basic Polish phrases can go a long way in making your stay more enjoyable. It shows respect for the local culture and can help you navigate daily life more easily.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Picking up a few basic Polish phrases can significantly enhance your stay. It demonstrates respect for the local culture and makes navigating daily life much easier.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: The most rewarding part of my exchange experience was definitely the friendships I formed. Meeting new people from different backgrounds and cultures enriched my time abroad and created lasting memories.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Language barriers, and being away from home. However, overcoming these challenges made the experience even more rewarding and helped me grow personally and academically.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
